vulnerability_analysis: The ByTradeToken contract has a flawed whenNotPaused modifier that allows the owner to bypass pause restrictions. The modifier checks `require(!paused || (msg.sender == owner()))`, which means if the sender is the owner, the check passes even when paused=true. This violates BEP20 standard as pause() should freeze ALL token transfers, not just non-owner transfers.
attack_strategy: As the attacker, we need to: 1) Impersonate the owner to call pause(), 2) Verify that regular users cannot transfer tokens while paused, 3) Show that the owner can still transfer tokens while paused, demonstrating the BEP20 violation.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Identify the owner address of the contract. 2. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 3. Call pause() to pause the contract. 4. Verify paused == true. 5. Show that a regular user cannot transfer tokens (should revert). 6. Show that the owner (still impersonated) CAN transfer tokens despite the pause. 7. The oracle expects paused == true, which we will achieve.
